requirements.summary: adduser created datauser (uid=1001, gid=1001) successfully and confirmed via `id`.

requirements.requirement: Limit datauser to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data
requirements.summary: A dedicated ext4 loopback filesystem was mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, and setquota applied a 102400 KB (100MB) soft=hard block limit for datauser, confirmed via repquota showing the limit attached to the user.

requirements.requirement: Quota must be enforced by the filesystem itself, not application-level
requirements.summary: As datauser, a 150MB dd write was stopped by the kernel at ~99MB with an EDQUOT ('Quota exceeded') error and nonzero exit code, directly demonstrating in-kernel ext4 quota enforcement rather than any application-layer restriction. This was reproduced identically after a full node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Quota configuration and enforcement persist across restart (durability of the setup)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id and healthy quota state were captured before restart, a reboot was issued and acknowledged, node1 became unreachable then returned with a distinctly different boot_id and near-zero uptime confirming an actual reboot, and after recovery /srv/data was automatically remounted with quota active, datauser's 100MB limit was intact per repquota, and the EDQUOT enforcement test reproduced the same failure behavior. This matches the independent boot-identity cross-check (af123507... -> 3214f5b4...).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were met: datauser was created, a filesystem-enforced 100MB quota was configured on /srv/data via a loopback ext4 filesystem with the modern in-kernel ext4 quota feature, kernel-level EDQUOT enforcement was directly demonstrated, and persistence across a real node restart (confirmed by a changed boot identity) was verified with recovered mount, quota configuration, and enforcement behavior. Minor hygiene issues exist (an abandoned aquota.user file from a superseded quota-file approach, and a reboot log file) but neither undermines functionality or security.
limitations: Command outputs are the only available evidence; no live inspection of node1 was possible to independently confirm current state beyond what was captured.

The lingering aquota.user file's exact effect (dormant vs. potentially confusing to a future administrator) could not be further probed since the executor did not run additional diagnostics on it after switching to the in-kernel quota feature.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two minor unnecessary residues remain from the task, both low-risk and non-functional. First, the executor initially attempted the deprecated external-quota-file approach (cmd-87ff608ffedd4f16, quotacheck -cum), which created /srv/data/aquota.user before the executor switched to the modern in-kernel ext4 quota feature via tune2fs -O quota (cmd-15b3913b8752416e). That now-unused aquota.user file was not removed and is still visible in /srv/data after the restart (cmd-bc8d4d8ad4c045c2) - an abandoned artifact from a corrected troubleshooting step, though harmless since the active quota mechanism is the in-kernel feature, not the file. Second, the reboot command redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log (cmd-2696732c9f234b5a), which persists as a new file confirmed by the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is an expected low-risk byproduct of the required restart evidence protocol rather than an unrelated mutation. No failed services, damaged package state, or weakened security controls were observed; package health and listening-socket changes between snapshots are attributable to the expected sshd/dhcpcd PID and DHCP-lease changes from the reboot itself.
